note:
The CHROME half of 2005 Bowman Draft Picks & Prospects, which BCP publishes as an <h3 id="Chrome"> subsection UNDER the paper page's Parallels heading rather than as its own page. That placement is why the scrape-bcp-ladders lane could never mint it: the lane reads Parallels rungs as parallels OF THE PAPER BASE SET and stops at Inserts, so the Chrome refractor ladder landed on bowman-draft-picks-and-prospects (the paper key) and the fifteen Chrome-only autograph CARD LINES were read as parallel NAMES -- the live catalog still holds hiq:baseball:2005:bowman-draft-picks-and-prospects:bdp129:bdp175-colby-rasmus-au-rc:no-auto as proof. Bowman and Bowman Chrome are DIFFERENT cards, so the Chrome stock gets its own key.

SETKEY IS THE EXISTING CONVENTION, NEVER A NEW SPELLING. bowman-chrome-draft-picks-and-prospects is already a productSetKeys entry (family bowman-chrome, parent bowman-draft-picks-and-prospects), is already a normalizeSetKey FIXED POINT, and is already the key the catalog carries for this product in 2002/2007/2008/2013. normalizeSetKey("Bowman Chrome Draft Picks & Prospects") returns it unchanged.

THE LADDER IS BCP'S, VERBATIM. "All 165 base cards are available in a Chrome parallel. The Chrome set, plus the fifteen First-Year Player Autographs, are available in the following Refractor parallels" -- Refractor (un-numbered; Autographs serial-numbered to 500), X-Fractor /250, Blue Refractor /150, Gold Refractor /50, Red Refractor 1/1, SuperFractor 1/1. The base Chrome card itself is emitted as the literal "Base" because it IS the checklist's base set, and the autograph rung carries printRun 500 on its Refractor exactly as BCP distinguishes it.

PRINTING PLATES ARE NOT EMITTED. BCP says only "set of four for each card" and names no plate colour; blank means unknown, never guessed, and four unnamed plates per card would be 720 synthetic rows.

AUTOS ARE FLAGGED FROM THE SECTION, NOT THE NAME. BDP166-BDP180 are isAuto=true because BCP's own heading states "These fifteen cards are all autographed and only available in the Chrome set" -- the checklist decides, not the "AU" token in the player string (feedback_isauto_boundary_is_cardnumber_not_text). BDP1-BDP165 stay isAuto=false. The trailing asterisks BCP prints on 48 base names and on BDP179/BDP180 are footnote markers (an unexplained BCP annotation, carried on no other source) and are stripped; "AU RC" is kept because that is how the sibling paper and bowman-chrome rows already spell these players.
